<br>

Let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be the parameters of our neural network. 

We have a differentiable loss function $\mathcal{L}: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ that tells us how good our model performs.

We want to find an update $\Delta \theta$, such that $\mathcal{L}(\theta + \Delta \theta) \leq \mathcal{L}(\theta)$.

In other words, we want to update our parameters $\theta^{(t+1)} \gets \theta^{(t)} + \Delta \theta^{(t)}$.

This can be formulated as
$$
\underset{\Delta \theta}{\operatorname{argmin}} \mathcal{L}(\theta + \Delta \theta)
$$

A Taylor expansion yields
$$
\mathcal{L}(\theta + \Delta \theta) = \mathcal{L}(\theta) + (\nabla_{\theta} \mathcal{L}(\theta))^T\Delta \theta + 
$$
